newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Rizal Bank main shareholder to raise stake.
newsitem.headline: Rizal Bank main shareholder to raise stake.

text.p: The Philippine Monetary Board has allowed Pan Malayan Management and Investment Corp to raise its stake in Rizal Commercial Banking Corp to 60 percent from 41 percent, Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said on Monday.
Pan Malayan is the investment arm of the family of Filipino-Chinese businessman Alfonso Yuchengo.
Reyes said Pan Malayan applied for the increase in stake following adoption of new rules which allow domestic corporations in existence for ten years to own up to 60 percent of a bank.
Earlier, there was a maximum limit of 30 percent.

The new privilege was granted to domestic investors when the Philippines in 1995 passed a law allowing ten foreign banks to come in and also gave foreign banks the option to own up to 60 percent of a local bank.

RCBC corporate Secretary Marcelo Dy told Reuters the bank is awaiting the Philippine Stock Exchange's advice on the record date of the bank's planned rights offer which will raise about 2.0 billion pesos.
He clarified that the case filed by the Antonino family at the Securities and Exchange Commission last December will not affect the rights offer.
The petition filed by by the Antoninos had sought to stop the planned public offering of RCBC shares following the rights offer.
The Antoninos, who own 12 percent of RCBC, had contended that their pre-emptive rights will be violated by the public offer.
The public offer, slated for this year, would raise 2.5 billion pesos, Dy said.
As of December 1996, the bank's total capital stock was 8.168 billion pesos, up from 6.850 billion pesos in 1995.
